intended_object: The fact (stored as `IsWeakLimit` data) that the chosen weak equalizer fork of `f, g : X ⟶ Y`, i.e. `Fork.ofι (weakEqualizer.ι f g) (weakEqualizer.condition f g)`, is a weak limit. In other words, every fork on `f, g` factors through it, though not necessarily uniquely. This comes from the docstring and from its analogy with Mathlib's `equalizerIsEqualizer`.
explanation: This declaration is really a lemma stored as data: it is the weak-limit version of the standard API declaration `CategoryTheory.Limits.equalizerIsEqualizer`. It takes the weak limit witness `weakLimit.isWeakLimit (parallelPair f g)` and moves it, along the isomorphism `Fork.ext (Iso.refl _)`, to the fork rebuilt from `weakEqualizer.ι`. That fork is the same cone up to that isomorphism, so the statement is exactly that the chosen weak equalizer is weakly limiting, which is what the docstring says. It works in an arbitrary category under the minimal hypothesis `HasWeakEqualizer f g`, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no other declaration making this statement; `equalizerIsEqualizer` is only the analogue for strong limits. It is a small API piece rather than a new concept, but it states the intended fact correctly and at full generality.
